source: Recalibrated for the updated 910C config from results/IRrecompute比例探究 and targeted task3 HSTU-small seq4096 bs4 W_IR/W_both retests.

npu_balance_model.definition: sum(core active_cycles) / (num_cores * max(core active_cycles)) from hardware_summary.csv
npu_balance_model.usage_note: Diagnostic from updated 910C IR sweep plus targeted W_IR/W_both retests. Batch-4 attention does not scale linearly across cores, but the current cost-model context lookup cannot distinguish hot/cold users, so global batch_gamma is left unchanged and context bounds are used instead.

ir_cost_model.source: Updated 910C IR selection calibration from layer kvcache preload timings and hardware_summary bandwidths.
notes: DDR KV preload bandwidth comes from hot W_IR/W_both HSTU-small seq4096 bs4 layer kvcache stages, which are about 45.3 GB/s even though whole-run DDR bandwidth is 40-43 GB/s.

SSD KV preload bandwidth uses the conservative 12.3 GB/s whole-run/read-bandwidth level from cold retests and IR sweep; kvcache-only stages can be higher but random history embedding lowers end-to-end SSD efficiency.
The minimum IR gain guard is 1% for updated 910C: W_both hot positive-k retests improved seq4096 bs4 by 2.15% and seq8192 bs1 by 3.13%, so the older 5% guard incorrectly clamped them to k=0.
compute_correction and batch_gamma are intentionally not overridden here: measured NPU core balance is poor and batch dependent, and the current context key does not include hot/cold user type.

W_IR.note: results/IRrecompute比例探究 continuous_80 was fastest at 0.961677 ms; continuous_100 regressed to 1.01709 ms, and random layouts were slower because history embedding preload became scattered.
Batch-4 W_IR cold retest with old k=1802 remained KV-preload dominated; use the sweep-derived 80% cap for this shape.

W_both.note: Targeted batch-4 W_both cold retest used k=1079 and completed in 2.05553 ms. W_both hot positive-k validation used k=181 for seq4096 bs4 and improved latency from 0.880261 ms to 0.861371 ms.
